import pandas as pd

# Read source CSV files with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_42/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_42/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_42/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_42/training_3.csv", index_col=0)

# All sources have the same schema and match the target schema columns (except order)
# The target schema order is:
# ['location': string, 'title': integer, 'company': integer, 'summary': integer, 'salary': integer, 'href': integer, 'rate': integer, 'reviews': integer, 'org_salary_period': integer]

# The sources have columns:
# ['title', 'company', 'location', 'summary', 'salary', 'href', 'rate', 'reviews', 'org_salary_period']

# We need to reorder columns to match target schema order:
# location, title, company, summary, salary, href, rate, reviews, org_salary_period

# Also, the target columns except location are integers.
# The source columns title, company, summary, salary, href, rate, reviews, org_salary_period are currently:
# - title, company, summary, salary, href, rate, reviews: numeric but may be string or float
# - org_salary_period: string (e.g., 'hour', 'month', 'year', 'day')

# From intermediate_step1.csv example, these columns are already converted to integers.
# So we will convert these columns to integers where possible.

# Concatenate all sources (union)
df = pd.concat([source0, source1, source2, source3], ignore_index=True)

# Reorder columns to target schema order
df = df[['location', 'title', 'company', 'summary', 'salary', 'href', 'rate', 'reviews', 'org_salary_period']]

# Convert numeric columns to integers
# Columns to convert: title, company, summary, salary, href, rate, reviews, org_salary_period
# But org_salary_period is string in source, target expects integer.
# From intermediate_step1.csv example, org_salary_period is integer-coded (e.g., 1,2,...)
# So we need to map org_salary_period string values to integers.

# Define mapping for org_salary_period based on source examples:
# observed values: 'hour', 'month', 'year', 'day'
# We assign integers as:
org_salary_period_map = {
    'hour': 1,
    'month': 2,
    'year': 3,
    'day': 4
}

# Map org_salary_period strings to integers, handle missing or unknown as NaN then fill with 0
df['org_salary_period'] = df['org_salary_period'].map(org_salary_period_map).fillna(0).astype(int)

# Convert other columns to integers
int_columns = ['title', 'company', 'summary', 'salary', 'href', 'rate', 'reviews']
for col in int_columns:
    # Some columns may have commas or be floats, convert safely
    # Remove commas if any, then convert to numeric, then to int
    df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col].astype(str).str.replace(',', ''), errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)

# The location column is string, keep as is

# Save the final dataframe to the target path
df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_42/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source CSV files with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_42/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_42/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_42/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
df3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_42/training_3.csv", index_col=0)

# Join all source tables on 'title' column (common column)
df01 = pd.merge(df0, df1, on='title', suffixes=('_0', '_1'), how='inner')
df012 = pd.merge(df01, df2, on='title', suffixes=('', '_2'), how='inner')
df_all = pd.merge(df012, df3, on='title', suffixes=('', '_3'), how='inner')

# After join, columns from different sources have suffixes, select and rename columns to match target schema:
# Target schema: ['location': string, 'title': integer, 'company': integer, 'summary': integer, 'salary': integer, 'href': integer, 'rate': integer, 'reviews': integer, 'org_salary_period': integer]

# For 'location', use from df0 (location_0)
# For other columns, aggregate max from all sources (to convert string columns to integer as in target, we use max aggregation)
# But location is string, so group by location

# Prepare a DataFrame with columns for aggregation
# Extract location from df0 (location_0)
df_all['location'] = df_all['location_0']

# Convert columns to numeric where possible (some columns may be string, convert to numeric for aggregation)
for col in ['company_0', 'company_1', 'company', 'company_2', 'company_3',
            'summary_0', 'summary_1', 'summary', 'summary_2', 'summary_3',
            'salary_0', 'salary_1', 'salary', 'salary_2', 'salary_3',
            'href_0', 'href_1', 'href', 'href_2', 'href_3',
            'rate_0', 'rate_1', 'rate', 'rate_2', 'rate_3',
            'reviews_0', 'reviews_1', 'reviews', 'reviews_2', 'reviews_3',
            'org_salary_period_0', 'org_salary_period_1', 'org_salary_period', 'org_salary_period_2', 'org_salary_period_3']:
    if col in df_all.columns:
        df_all[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_all[col], errors='coerce')

# Aggregate max for each attribute from all sources
df_all['company'] = df_all[['company_0', 'company_1', 'company', 'company_2', 'company_3']].max(axis=1)
df_all['summary'] = df_all[['summary_0', 'summary_1', 'summary', 'summary_2', 'summary_3']].max(axis=1)
df_all['salary'] = df_all[['salary_0', 'salary_1', 'salary', 'salary_2', 'salary_3']].max(axis=1)
df_all['href'] = df_all[['href_0', 'href_1', 'href', 'href_2', 'href_3']].max(axis=1)
df_all['rate'] = df_all[['rate_0', 'rate_1', 'rate', 'rate_2', 'rate_3']].max(axis=1)
df_all['reviews'] = df_all[['reviews_0', 'reviews_1', 'reviews', 'reviews_2', 'reviews_3']].max(axis=1)
df_all['org_salary_period'] = df_all[['org_salary_period_0', 'org_salary_period_1', 'org_salary_period', 'org_salary_period_2', 'org_salary_period_3']].max(axis=1)

# 'title' is integer in target, use from df0 (title)
df_all['title'] = df_all['title']

# Select only target columns
result = df_all[['location', 'title', 'company', 'summary', 'salary', 'href', 'rate', 'reviews', 'org_salary_period']]

# Group by 'location' and aggregate max for other columns (to match target aggregation)
result = result.groupby('location', as_index=False).agg({
    'title': 'max',
    'company': 'max',
    'summary': 'max',
    'salary': 'max',
    'href': 'max',
    'rate': 'max',
    'reviews': 'max',
    'org_salary_period': 'max'
})

# Write to target CSV
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_42/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
